We have a PDB file with coordinates for residues A1 to A100. The question: find protein heavy atom (i.e., non-hydrogen atom) that is closest to K54:NZ. Excluding the K54 itself and any atom directly attached to K54 (i.e., side chain atoms bonded to NZ). K54 is Lysine at position 54 (A:K54). The NZ atom is the terminal nitrogen of side chain. Atoms attached to NZ: The Lys side chain has NZ bonded to CB? Actually Lysine side chain: N-terminus? Let's recall: Lysine has side chain: N (CA) - CB - CG - CD - CE - NZ (or NZ?). In standard Lys: CA - CB - CG - CD - CE - NZ. Actually Lys: CA-CB-CG-CD-CE-NZ. So atoms directly attached to NZ: CE (the carbon) is bonded to NZ. So atoms within one covalent bond from NZ: CE and CA? Wait, NZ is terminal nitrogen. It is bonded to CE (the carbon). So CE is directly attached (one bond). Also maybe the hydrogen attached to NZ (but hydrogen not heavy atom). So we exclude A:K54:NZ and any atom connected to it by one or two covalent bonds. "Excluding A:K54:NZ itself and any atom connected to it by one or two covalent bonds". So exclude atoms that are directly bonded to NZ (i.e., CE) and maybe also atoms two bonds away? "one or two covalent bonds" means any atom that is within two bonds from NZ. So exclude atoms up to distance of two bonds away from NZ (i.e., NZ itself, CE, and maybe CA? Actually CA is two bonds away: NZ-CE-CB? Wait, chain: NZ - CE - CD - CG - CB - CA. So CA is five bonds away. So not excluded. But the rule says exclude any atom connected to it by one or two covalent bonds. That includes atoms directly bonded (one bond) and also atoms that are two bonds away? The phrase "connected to it by one or two covalent bonds" suggests any atom that is within two bonds of NZ. So we should exclude atoms that are at bond distances of 1 or 2 from NZ. Let's interpret: For Lys side chain, the atoms within two bonds from NZ: NZ (bond 0), CE (bond 1), CD (bond 2). Also maybe the hydrogen atoms (not heavy). So we exclude A:K54:NZ, A:K54:CE, A:K54:CD. Also maybe the oxygen? Actually Lys side chain has no oxygen. So we need to find the closest heavy atom among all other residues (including other residues) that is not any of those atoms.

Thus we need to compute distances between NZ (K54) and all other heavy atoms in the structure, ignoring those atoms that are within 2 bonds of NZ (i.e., NZ, CE, CD). Then find the minimum distance.
